blocks.text: Second, lest it be asked how Samson's bees could have touched the flesh of a carcass or endured its foul smell, since bees shrink from both, I say that what is here called a carcass was rather a σκελετὸν σῶμα [skeleton sōma], a dried and withered body, in which nothing remained but the framework of the bones. So the Syriac translator takes it, who rendered ܫܠܕܐ ܓܪܡܢܝܐ, that is, a bony carcass, or, what is the same, a σκελετόν [skeleton]. This interpretation is favoured by the fact that the lion's carcass had lain on the ground for a long time. For Samson, who had killed it, left it lying in the field, וישב מימים, and he returned after days (so it reads literally) to take Delilah, and he turned aside to see the carcass of that lion. After days: that is, after a year. So the Hebrews take it in this passage, and so it is used throughout Scripture. Thus Gen. IV, 3. And it came to pass מקץ ימים, at the end of days: that is, at the end of a year. Genes. XXIV, 55. Let the girl remain with us ימים או עשר, days, or ten: that is, a year, or ten months. Levit. XXV, 29. If someone sells a house, etc. ימים תהיה גאלתו, for days shall be its redemption: that is, the right of redeeming it shall last for a year, until שנה תמימה, a full year, is completed: as is explained in the following verse. Iudic. XI, 4. And it came to pass after days (that is, after a year) that the Ammonites made war against the Israelites. And vers. 40. מימים ימימה, From days to days (that is, from year to year, in one word annually) the daughters of Israel went to lament the daughter of Jephthah. As in 1 Sam. I, 3. That man went up from days to days to worship in Shiloh: that is, שנה בשנה, annually, as is explained in vers. 7. And in vers. 20 of the same chapter: In the revolution of days (that is, of a year) Hannah conceived and bore a son. And II, 19. To offer the sacrifice of days, that is, the yearly one. And XXVII, 7. And the number of days that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was ימים וארבעה חדשים, days (that is, a year) and four months. Nothing is more frequent than this expression. Therefore, when Samson is said to have returned after days, etc., it is the same as if it were said that only after a year did he return and turn aside to see the carcass of the lion killed a year before ^{(3)}. From [III, 358] this it is therefore probable that nothing but the bones remained, since time had consumed the flesh, or wild beasts had devoured it. In such a skeleton, then, why could a swarm of bees not have settled and made its honey, as in the head of Onesilus hung at the gate of Amathus? For so Herodotus has it, book 5, ch. 114: Ὀνησίλου μὲν Ἀμαθούσιοι, ὅτι σφέας ἐπολιόρκησε, ἀποταμόντες τὴν κεφαλὴν, ἐκόμι- [col. 506] σαν εἰς Ἀμαθοῦντα, καὶ μιν ἀπεκρέμασαν ὑπὲρ τῶν πυλέων· κρεμαμένης δὲ τῆς κεφαλῆς, καὶ ἔσης ἤδη κοίλης, ἐσμὸς μελισσέων, ἐσδὺς ἐς αὐτὴν, κηρίων μιν ἐνέπλησε· [Onēsilou men Amathousioi, hoti spheas epoliorkēse, apotamontes tēn kephalēn, ekomisan eis Amathounta, kai min apekremasan hyper tōn pyleōn; kremamenēs de tēs kephalēs, kai esēs ēdē koilēs, esmos melisseōn, esdys es autēn, kēriōn min eneplēse] The Amathusians cut off the head of Onesilus, because he had besieged them, and, having carried it to Amathus, hung it above the gates. And when it, hanging there, had already become hollow, a swarm of bees entered it and filled it with honeycombs. And in the tomb of Hippocrates, if we believe Soranus in his Life, μέχρι πολλοῦ σμῆνος ἦν ἐργαζόμενον μέλι [mechri pollou smēnos ēn ergazomenon meli], there was for a long time a swarm of bees making honey. Nor is it unlike what I have read in Aldrovandi, book 1 On Insects, page 110: that at Verona, in the church of the Holy Cross, in the tomb of the sisters of the distinguished jurist Bartholomaeus Vitalis, one of whom had died in the year 1558 and the other in 1562, bees made honeycombs abundantly between the two carcasses, until in the year 1566 the tomb was opened by lightning, without any damage either to the carcasses or to the honeycombs, and displayed before everyone the honeycombs themselves and the bees making honey in great numbers.
